previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: The patient was admitted for severe recurrent major depression with psychotic features and suicidal ideation, complicated by chronic pain, opioid dependence, and chronic pancreatitis. She presented with profound hopelessness and a history of self-harm, but engaged in treatment during her stay. Psychiatric medications were optimized with the addition of quetiapine to address psychotic symptoms and improve sleep, while continuing sertraline, mirtazapine, and methadone with therapeutic drug monitoring. A J-tube malfunction was corrected on admission, and radiographic imaging confirmed proper placement in the jejunum. The patient participated in counseling, reported reduced suicidal thoughts, and denied active self-harm ideation by discharge. She was stabilized, educated on medication and J-tube care, and discharged with outpatient follow-up for psychiatry and pain management. Allergies to milk and other foods were documented and addressed in care planning.

that point, her medications were tapered first from IV dilaudid 
to PO tramadol (although she requested that the IV dilaudid 
remain written for while transitioning to PO tramadol), then IV 
ativan to PO, then IV benadryl to PO hydroxyzine.  She requested 
that her IV phenergan remain written for until discharge.  It is 
noted that IV benadryl and IV phenergan can both potentiate 
narcotic euphoria.  She was not discharged on narcotics, and 
should NEVER be discharged from this point forward on any

her outpatient pain management provider ___.  Any future 
abdominal pain admissions should include consultation with ___.

multiple suicide attempts in the past while in the hospital 
(when not provided narcotics), her psychiatric status was 
monitored closely.  She did not display any signs of 
suicidality.  She did threaten to leave AMA at one point 
initially when her narcotics were not written as she requested 
(2mg Q3 hours IV dilaudid).  Her home psychiatric medications 
were continued throughout the admission.  
.

provider's note and her last discharge summary all list 
different variations on her medications.  In addition, the
